extracted.intended_audience: Members of Congress, committee staff, legal counsel, litigants, journalists, and the general public interested in Purdue Pharma/Sackler oversight and opioid accountability
extracted.subtask_description: Official House Oversight and Reform Committee transcript of a December 17, 2020 hearing on Purdue Pharma and the Sackler family, containing sworn oral statements, questions, procedural rulings, and agreed document/disclosure commitments. Useful for monitoring testimony, disclosure obligations, and accountability measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath / Truthfulness of Testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Witnesses are sworn to tell "the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral testimony given under oath is part of the official record and witnesses are legally bound to be truthful when answering committee questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Testimony Part of the Record
rubrics_metrics.description: "Without objection, your written testimonies and statements will be part of the record."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepared/written statements submitted by witnesses are included in the official hearing record and made publicly available via House repositories (docs.house.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary Appearance and Subpoena Status
rubrics_metrics.description: Witnesses may appear voluntarily "without the need for subpoenas."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee acknowledges and values voluntary cooperation; appearance without subpoena is noted and can affect public and procedural posture but does not waive later document requests or inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of Additional Materials and QFRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Members have five legislative days to submit additional materials and written questions for the witnesses (Questions for the Record – QFRs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Witnesses are asked to respond promptly to QFRs; documents entered into the record and QFR responses are made available via committee repositories and become part of the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to Produce Documents and Accountings
rubrics_metrics.description: Witnesses (here, the Sackler family) agreed to provide a full accounting of shell companies and to make publicly available all documents in their possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee expects full transparency and document disclosure; the transcript records commitments to produce asset/accounting information and other documents responsive to committee requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board Fiduciary Oversight and Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The board received regular documented reports from management (including from former DEA professionals and former Federal prosecutors) confirming programs were functioning and that the company was complying with law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards are expected to receive, review, and act on compliance and risk reports; outside directors and the board's oversight role are emphasized as part of accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate Compliance Program Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Purdue "instituted a strict compliance program that was designed to ensure that Purdue in its marketing complied with all laws."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An effective compliance program should be instituted, monitored, and documented; management should regularly report program effectiveness to the board and independent auditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abuse and Diversion Detection Program (ADD Program)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purdue maintained an Abuse and Diversion Detection Program that kept detailed records on prescribers; the program purportedly reported over 200 doctors to authorities but critics said only a small fraction of 'Region Zero' prescribers were reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A credible ADD program should (1) keep detailed prescribing data, (2) identify high-volume or suspicious prescribers, (3) escalate and report confirmed concerns to law enforcement/medical boards, and (4) ensure remedial actions are effective and timely. The transcript highlights deficiencies (timeliness, low reporting rate, and circumvention by marketing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do-Not-Call / Region Zero Controls and Enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Purdue used a 'Region Zero' list to indicate prescribers who should not be contacted by sales reps; documented problems included lack of timely reporting and loopholes allowing sales tactics to continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do-not-contact lists or restrictions must be enforced strictly (no contacting practice colleagues, pharmacies, or other circumventions); failure to enforce undermines risk mitigation efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Misleading Marketing and False Narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Purdue was accused of creating "false advertising documents" and promoting narratives that minimized addiction risk and steered patients away from safer alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketing and promotional materials must be truthful, not minimize risks, and not incentivize prescribing through deceptive claims or false safety assurances; companies must avoid messaging that blames patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Illegal Kickbacks and Fraudulent Promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: The company pleaded guilty to misbranding, conspiracy to defraud the U.S., and illegal kickbacks related to marketing OxyContin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies must not pay or structure incentives that constitute kickbacks or illegal steering; violations carry criminal liability, fines, and long-term oversight obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product Safety and Abuse-Deterrent Formulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Purdue developed what it described as the first abuse-deterrent OxyContin formulation that could not be easily crushed, snorted, or dissolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pharmaceutical companies are expected to pursue product designs that reduce abuse potential where feasible and to publicly describe harm-reduction steps taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability Through Financial Remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Witnesses discussed dedicating billions, relinquishing interest in the company, and dedicating Purdue's assets to a public benefit company to abate addiction and provide treatment/overdose-reversal medicines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaningful restitution includes financial contributions, transfer of assets to restorative entities, and commitments that ensure victims and affected communities receive resources quickly and at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of Fraudulent Transfers (UFTA Standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the Uniform Fraudulent Transfer Act, section 4(a)(2): making a transfer without receiving reasonably equivalent value when the debtor could not pay debts as they became due may constitute a fraudulent transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large distributions to insiders that reduce assets available to creditors may be clawed back in bankruptcy under fraudulent transfer principles; banks/insiders must consider creditors' interests when moving large sums from an insolvent or potentially-insolvent entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory Debtor-in-Possession Fiduciary Duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1107 the company's management (debtor in possession) has fiduciary duties similar to a trustee to maximize recoveries for creditors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debtor-in-possession must pursue recoveries (including litigation and clawbacks) for creditors and cooperate with creditors and the bankruptcy process to preserve and distribute assets lawfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with DOJ and Transparency via Public Repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: Purdue committed to ongoing cooperation with the Department of Justice and to creating a public repository for documents deemed relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperating with investigators and making relevant documents public facilitates accountability; repositories should be accessible so the public and authorities can review relevant records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cessation of Harmful Commercial Practices (Sales Promotion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedial action cited: ending promotion of opioid products by sales representatives (action taken by Purdue ~2017).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stopping aggressive sales promotion of high-risk products is a concrete mitigation step; companies should review and, if necessary, suspend promotional activities that materially contribute to public harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Apology and Acceptance of Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Both company leadership and family members were expected/urged to acknowledge wrongdoing, apologize, and take responsibility (CEO: "I'm profoundly sorry"; Chair: asked Sacklers to "acknowledge your wrongdoing").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public acknowledgment and apology are part of restorative accountability; coupled with tangible remedial actions and transparency, they form part of public expectations for corporate responsibility.
